title: Client surface evolution: stability adapters for resumable streaming and cursor semantics
creator: Riley Patel
description: PRD-level requirements and acceptance criteria for evolving the Redwood SDK client surfaces (Python/TypeScript/Go) to provide a stability adapter layer that: 1) defines explicit cursor pagination semantics, 2) standardizes resumable streaming APIs with deterministic reconnection and idempotency semantics, and 3) clarifies retry/interruption behavior for cross-version interoperability. Goal: reduce integration regressions, make backwards compatibility guarantees explicit, and provide client helpers to reduce incorrect consumer implementations.
background: Customers and internal integrators have reported subtle breakages when the server-side stream framing, cursor formats, and backoff hooks evolve. Multiple incidents were due to: (a) clients interpreting opaque cursors differently after server upgrades, (b) retries causing duplicate side effects when calls were not idempotent, and (c) streaming reconnections producing inconsistent partial state across SDK versions. The SDKs currently expose low-level primitives with library-specific idioms, leading to variance in behavior across languages.
proposal_summary: Introduce a small, language-consistent 'stability adapter' layer in each SDK that provides: a stable Cursor type with version metadata and validation helpers; a ResumableStream abstraction with semantic guarantees (exactly-once event delivery for idempotent operations, at-least-once for non-idempotent, clearly surfaced); consistent RetryPolicy defaults (transparent jittered exponential backoff with optional idempotency token injection); and migration helpers for older cursor formats. The adapter is opt-in by default but will be recommended in docs and templates.
api_surface: For each SDK we will add: 1) Cursor.parse(cursorString) -> Cursor (structured with fields: v, token, meta) and Cursor.serialize(), 2) ResumableStream.open(request, options) -> ResumableStream with methods: resumeFrom(Cursor), on(event, handler), close(), snapshotCursor(), 3) ClientConfig.retryPolicy defaults with fields: maxAttempts, initialBackoffMs, maxBackoffMs, jitterFactor, idempotencyHeaderName, 4) helpers: makeIdempotent(request, idempotencyKey) and migration.convertLegacyCursor(cursorString). Documentation will include language examples for Python/TS/Go.
pagination_contracts: Define two pagination modes: Cursor-based (preferred) and Offset-based (legacy). Cursor format must be considered opaque by consumers; Cursor.parse will expose a stable minimal surface: versionTag (string), payload (opaque base64), safeHint (optional string). Server guarantees: cursors minted by runtime vN must be parseable by runtime vN+K where K >= 2. Acceptance tests will assert forward-parse capability across minor runtime releases. Migration helper will surface a deprecation warning when legacy offset tokens are used and provide conversion when possible.
streaming_contracts: ResumableStream semantic guarantees: - Open+stream produces a monotonic sequence of event IDs; server must provide lastAckedId in stream frames. - resumeFrom(cursor) semantics: server will accept cursor payloads issued by compatible runtime versions and return a resume token and the first next event id. - Delivery semantics: For idempotent operations the SDK will expose exactly-once semantics by deduplicating events using event ID and an idempotency token header. For non-idempotent operations the SDK will expose at-least-once behavior and require explicit client-side dedup where needed. - Cancellation: close() sends a best-effort cancellation frame and does not assume server immediate stop. - Timeouts: SDK default per-chunk timeout and an overall stream heartbeat policy will be standardized.
retry_policy: Default RetryPolicy: maxAttempts=5, initialBackoffMs=100, maxBackoffMs=5000, jitterFactor=0.25, retryableCodes=[429,502,503,504], nonRetryableCodes=[400,401,403], idempotencyHeaderName='x-rw-idempotency-key'. SDK helper makeIdempotent will attach a v4 UUID header when developer opts-in. Retries for streaming reconnection will honor resumeFrom(cursor) where available; otherwise stream will restart from beginning only if the request is marked idempotent.
compatibility_and_degradation: Compatibility rules: - Public SDKs must preserve Cursor and ResumableStream shapes for two minor releases. - New optional fields may be added to Cursor payloads; parsers must ignore unknown keys. - If an adapter detects an incompatible server version, it will surface a clear error 'IncompatibleCursorVersion' with remediation steps. - Degradation policy: SDKs will provide a 'compatibility fallback' mode to switch to non-resumable streaming (stateless polling) with explicit telemetry when server signals incompatibility. - Breaking change policy requires feature flag gating and rollout with console rollout rules.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: library-level implementation + unit tests (2 cycles). Phase 2: integration tests against staging runtime matrix (runtime versions -1..+1) + language SDK smoke tests (1 cycle). Phase 3: opt-in beta release to customers and internal teams (2 weeks), collect telemetry. Phase 4: enable recommended behavior by default in minor release after no critical regressions for 4 weeks. Each phase must produce a migration doc, changelog entry, and example code samples.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs provide Cursor.parse and Cursor.serialize in Python/TS/Go with consistent field names and behavior
ResumableStream can successfully resume from cursor across runtime minor versions in integration tests (tested matrix: server v1.18..1.20)
RetryPolicy defaults applied uniformly and documented; at least one SDK uses makeIdempotent helper in default codegen examples
Backward-compatibility tests demonstrating parsing of legacy offset tokens using migration.convertLegacyCursor when possible
End-to-end demo: client opens a stream, disconnects mid-stream, and resumes without duplicate side effects for idempotent operations
Telemetry: SDK emits structured events for resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_failure, compatibility_fallback with schema documented
Docs: migration guide, API reference, and three runnable examples (one per language) exist in the public docs site
No high-severity regressions observed during 2-week beta with 5 internal customers
test_cases: unit: Cursor roundtrip preserves versionTag and payload for valid tokens and rejects malformed tokens with parse errors
integration: streaming resume test under network partition where server returns lastAckedId and stream resumes with no duplicates for idempotent requests
compat: server introduces optional cursor field; older SDK parses and ignores extra field
retry: forced 503 errors cause exponential backoff and eventual success within maxAttempts when idempotency token present
degradation: incompatible cursor version triggers compatibility_fallback mode and telemetry event
open_questions: Should the idempotency helper be injected automatically for common read-like endpoints or left opt-in for all write endpoints?
What is the minimum server-side cursor version support guarantee we can make for Dedicated vs Hosted deployments?
Is it acceptable to expose lastAckedId in stream frames for privacy-sensitive customers, or should it be opt-in?
notes: Implementation owners: SDK leads for python (Anika Shah), ts (Morgan Lee), go (Diego Fernandez). Engineering will add runtime stubs for resume semantics. PM to coordinate beta with two high-volume customers to validate cost and latency impact. Keep adapter layer small and well-tested; prefer clear errors instead of hidden heuristics.
